title: Specialized Tarmac SL8 Pro 6 Month Review - I HATE That I LOVE This Bike...

takeaways.text: The Pro with Ultegra Di2 cost just over £8,000 at publication, £4,000 less than the S-Works he rode the year before.
Around his test track it was not as fast as a Canyon Aeroad or BMC Teammachine R, but in the same company as a Van Rysel or SEKA Spear.

In his UK range the S-Works, Pro and Expert share the frame design, tube shapes and aero profile; only the S-Works gets a lighter carbon lay-up, about 6.7 kg built against roughly 7.2 kg for the Pro tested.
Low weight, stiffness, steep angles and a short wheelbase gave it a lively, whippy feel on climbs, yet it stayed comfortable enough for 100-mile rides on rough roads.

The Pro's one-piece bar was 42 cm wide on his size 56, and Specialized's website offered no bar-width or stem-length choice; he would pick the Expert, which has the same frame and a two-piece bar and stem.
After six months in all weathers he reported no issues: shifting never needed indexing, and brakes, bottom bracket, hubs and headset were still smooth.

disclosure: The video does not say how the bike was obtained. It includes a sponsored segment for Insta360, and the description carries affiliate links.
summary: An August 2025 six-month review of a Tarmac SL8 Pro with Ultegra Di2 on the SL8 frame that, below S-Works, uses FACT 10r carbon like the Comp recorded here. It covers the range structure, ride, fit and reliability; the Pro's groupset, wheels, one-piece cockpit and price differ from the Comp 105 Di2.
